adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:479 — isAccessTokenId` uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` to read the grant-type shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider documents/encodes it at indices 4-6 (chars 5-6), so the matcher compares against the wrong 2-char window (tail of tokenType shortcut + first char of grantType shortcut) and will never validate the actual grant shortcut.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, it extracts the grant shortcut via items[0].substring(3, 5), but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes token IDs as 2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType (length 6), so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6 (0-based). Using (3,5) reads the last char of tokenType plus first char of grantType, so it cannot correctly match the intended 2-char grant shortcut. Additionally, the matcher logic is inverted: `if (substring.equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, so even a correct extraction would reject matching shortcuts. This makes the test validation incorrect/broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1051 — Access token "jti"/id format changes from a plain UUID to a prefixed "ssttgt:uuid" string, an externally-visible token claim (also surfaced in admin/event "tokenId" details per AssertEvents.java changes) that third-party clients, event listeners, or systems doing UUID.fromString/DB lookups on the raw jti may now fail to parse.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes access token ID generation from `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (UUID-like) to an encoded value via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` that prefixes context and a colon (`<6 chars>:<rawTokenId>`) in `TokenManager.initToken` (services/.../TokenManager.java). Tests are updated to expect this new `Details.TOKEN_ID` format (AssertEvents now calls `isAccessTokenId(...)`), indicating the change is intentional, not an accidental defect. However, it is an externally-visible, backwards-incompatible change to the `jti`/token ID claim and event/admin details that could break consumers expecting a plain UUID, so it’s a legitimate review concern but not a verifiable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29 — New abstract method getShortcut() added to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI with no default implementation, breaking binary/source compatibility for any third-party/custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java) without a `default` implementation. Any existing third-party/custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation would no longer compile and would also fail binary compatibility (NoSuchMethodError/AbstractMethodError depending on linkage) unless updated, so the finding is a real compatibility concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:99 — Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) was removed; any extension code that relied on cloning a Context via this constructor will fail to compile against the new SPI version.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java` removes the previously existing `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor (the entire constructor block is deleted). This is an SPI/API compatibility break: any external/extension code that compiled against this SPI and used `new OAuth2GrantType.Context(existingContext)` will now fail to compile. This is a real, diff-grounded concern, but it’s not a functional runtime defect introduced by the change itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84 — getShouldUseLightweightToken visibility widened from package-private to public static, which is source-compatible but permanently exposes formerly-internal logic as public API surface on an abstract class subclassed by custom protocol mappers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession)` from package-private to `public static` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java). This does widen visibility and makes the method callable by external/custom protocol mappers (the class is commonly extended), increasing the exposed API surface. That’s an architectural/API-surface concern rather than a correctness defect, and it is directly grounded in the change shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:53 — getTokenContextFromTokenId tolerates legacy plain-UUID token ids (no colon) for backward compatibility, but this compatibility path is undocumented and relies on grantType being silently set to UNKNOWN/"na", which could affect any downstream logic keyed on decoded grant type for tokens issued before upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a backward-compatibility decode path in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`: if no `:` is present, it returns an `AccessTokenContext` with `SessionType.UNKNOWN`, `TokenType.UNKNOWN`, and grant type `UNKNOWN` ("na"). That behavior is real and currently not explained in code/Javadoc beyond implicit logic, so the “undocumented/silent UNKNOWN grantType for legacy token IDs” concern is diff-grounded. However, the claimed downstream behavioral impact is speculative from the diff alone (no downstream logic keyed on decoded grant type is shown), so it’s not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:226 — The encoded-context length "6" and the substring offsets (0,2 / 2,4 / 4,6) are hardcoded magic numbers instead of derived from named constants tied to SessionType/TokenType/grant shortcut lengths, so any future shortcut-length change silently breaks parsing.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId the parsing logic assumes a fixed 6-character context header and fixed 2-character segments via hardcoded values (length==6, substrings (0,2),(2,4),(4,6)). While current SessionType/TokenType shortcuts and the grant shortcuts added in this diff are all 2 chars (e.g., "on","rt","ac"), the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut contract explicitly allows other shortcut lengths ("usually like 3-letters"), so a future change to any shortcut length would silently make this parser reject or mis-parse token IDs. This is a real maintainability/robustness issue introduced by the change, but not an immediate correctness bug given the current shortcuts in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:322 — grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are package-private (no access modifier) rather than private, existing only so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest can reach in and mutate production state directly instead of going through a constructor/setter API.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` declaring `Map<String, String> grantsByShortcuts;` and `Map<String, String> grantsToShortcuts;` with no access modifier, making them package-private. The new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` (same package `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.encode`) directly assigns/mutates these fields (`factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>(); ... factory.grantsToShortcuts = ...`) instead of using a constructor/setter/test hook API. This is a real encapsulation/testing-architecture concern introduced by the change, but not a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:351 — postInit reaches into the OAuth2GrantType SPI (factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)) to build its shortcut maps, coupling the token-context-encoder SPI's initialization order and correctness to another SPI's factories being registered first, which is implicit and easy to break when adding new SPIs or reordering init.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(KeycloakSessionFactory) iterating over `factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` to build `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts`, and later relying on `sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType)` and scanning factories to resolve shortcuts. This is a concrete cross-SPI dependency introduced by the change (token-context-encoder SPI depends on OAuth2GrantType factories/shortcuts being available), which is an architectural/initialization-order coupling concern. However, the diff alone does not prove this causes broken behavior in Keycloak’s SPI lifecycle (postInit may already run after all factories are registered), so it’s not verifiable as a defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:219 — getTokenContextFromTokenId uses the raw literal ':' as the delimiter between encoded context and raw token id with no shared constant, duplicated with the concatenation in encodeTokenId (line 268), so the two must be kept in sync by convention only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show both parsing and encoding use the literal ':' delimiter (indexOf(':') in getTokenContextFromTokenId and ':' + rawTokenId in encodeTokenId), but this is a maintainability/style suggestion rather than a verifiable defect or significant review issue. Both sides currently match, so no broken behavior is introduced by the diff solely due to not using a shared constant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1051 — initToken calls encoder.encodeTokenId() with no try/catch; if a custom/plugin OAuth2GrantTypeFactory's postInit failed or a grant type has no registered shortcut, encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException uncaught, causing every token issuance for that flow to fail with an unhandled 500 instead of a controlled OAuth error response

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TokenManager.initToken() now always encodes the access token ID via TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...) with no local handling of IllegalStateException. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will throw if the grant type has no known shortcut (grantShort == null). While built-in grant factories added in this diff implement getShortcut() and the provider maps UNKNOWN->UNKNOWN, a misbehaving/custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (e.g., returning null/duplicate shortcut) could make grantShort null and cause token issuance to fail via an uncaught runtime exception at this call site. However, the claim about “postInit failed” causing this at runtime isn’t verifiable from the diff (postInit failure would typically prevent startup), and whether this should be translated to an OAuth error vs. fail-fast is an architectural/robustness concern rather than a definite core defect for normal configurations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:60 — getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for malformed/wrong-length prefixes or unknown shortcuts; this method is not yet invoked from introspection/refresh/revocation endpoints, but is designed to be, and no caller in the codebase currently wraps/catches it, so a future or missed wiring will surface as an unhandled 500 rather than an invalid_token error for old/garbled tokens

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId` explicitly throws `IllegalArgumentException` for malformed IDs (no `:` is handled as “old token”, but wrong context length or unknown shortcuts throws). The diff does not show any current caller that invokes this decode path in introspection/refresh/revocation (TokenManager only *encodes* token IDs via `encodeTokenId(...)`). So the claim of an existing unhandled-500 bug cannot be verified from current wiring. However, the new API does introduce a sharp edge: any future/added caller that decodes arbitrary/attacker-controlled token IDs without catching this exception would turn invalid input into a 500 rather than a controlled invalid-token response. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/contract concern rather than a proven current defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:73 — postInit throws IllegalStateException on shortcut/id collisions across OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations, which aborts factory initialization at server startup/deploy time; a third-party or community grant-type provider whose getShortcut() collides with a built-in or another plugin will crash server boot with no fallback, turning an upgrade/deployment of a new provider into a full outage rather than disabling just that provider

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the code populates grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts using Map.put() and then throws IllegalStateException if the map sizes differ (duplicate shortcut or duplicate grant id causes overwrites and size mismatch). This exception is thrown during postInit (server boot/deploy SPI initialization), so a colliding third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation would indeed abort initialization with no fallback/disable-path shown in the diff. This is a robustness/extension-compatibility concern rather than a clear correctness defect in the core logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:108 — encodeTokenId's IllegalStateException can be triggered at runtime (not just startup) when a grant type is dynamically deployed after postInit ran without triggering the map refresh correctly, or when a grant session attribute (Constants.GRANT_TYPE) is set to a value with no matching OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (e.g. legacy/custom code paths setting an arbitrary string) — token issuance then fails hard instead of degrading gracefully (e.g. falling back to the UNKNOWN shortcut)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a hard failure path during token issuance: `TokenManager.initToken()` now encodes the token ID via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throws `IllegalStateException` when `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` returns null (i.e., grant type not mapped). While `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` falls back to `UNKNOWN` only when the session attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is null, it does not protect against the attribute being set to a non-null value that has no matching `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`/shortcut. This is a resilience/compatibility concern for custom/legacy code paths that might set `ClientSessionContext` attributes arbitrarily, but the diff does not prove that core/standard flows will set an unmapped value, so it’s not a clearly verifiable defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:112 — getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily refresh grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts via unsynchronized read-check-then-put on ConcurrentHashMap; concurrent requests hitting an unresolved grant type simultaneously each redundantly call sessionFactory.getProviderFactory, which is only a minor inefficiency, not corruption, but there is no negative-result caching so every request for a genuinely-unknown/unregistered grant type re-scans providers on the hot token-issuance path

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut the code does a ConcurrentHashMap get(), then if null performs an expensive lookup (sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(...) or scanning getProviderFactoriesStream(...)) and then put(). This is a non-atomic read-check-then-act pattern, so concurrent callers can redundantly perform the expensive lookup for the same missing entry. Additionally, if a grant type/shortcut is genuinely unknown, there is no negative-result caching, so every call will repeat the expensive lookup on the hot token-encoding path (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId -> factory.getShortcutByGrantType). This is a performance/architecture concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Context.grantType is populated directly from the untrusted form parameter formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) and later encoded into the token id; relies on upstream dispatch already validating it matches a registered grant provider id, so no independent revalidation happens before encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException on mismatch (fail-closed, but worth confirming dispatch always uses exact-match lookup)

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `OAuth2GrantType.Context` stores `grantType` directly from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)` and this value is later copied into `ClientSessionContext` (`OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, also in some other grant flows) and used by `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()`, which will throw `IllegalStateException` if the grant type is not known to `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`'s maps. The diff itself does not show any local revalidation/sanitization of `context.getGrantType()` before encoding, so the behavior depends on the upstream grant dispatch always invoking the matching provider for the given `grant_type`. This is an architectural/defense-in-depth concern rather than a demonstrable defect from the diff alone.
